title: Scraper: Gigabyte Server (EPYC MZ-series)
description:

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Scraper for Gigabyte server motherboards. Distinct from the existing consumer Gigabyte scraper — server BIOSes live under a different URL tree and product hierarchy.

board_class: EPYC.

Sockets: SP3 (MZ31-AR0, MZ32-AR0), SP5 (MZ33-AR0/AR1, MZ73-LM0/LM1), SP6 (MZ34-AR0 and similar Siena boards).

Access strategy:
- Catalog: https://www.gigabyte.com/Enterprise/Server-Motherboard?fid=2816 (AMD filter). Lists MZ-prefixed boards by socket family.
- Per-board page: https://www.gigabyte.com/Enterprise/Server-Motherboard/{MODEL}-rev-{rev}/support#support-dl-bios — same support tab pattern as the consumer scraper.
- Same Akamai Bot Manager protection as consumer www.gigabyte.com — reuse the existing _HEADERS dict from src/psp_etl/scrape/gigabyte.py (browser User-Agent + Sec-Fetch + sec-ch-ua headers). CDN download.gigabyte.com is unprotected once the URL is known.

Implementation notes:
- Heavy code overlap with consumer GigabyteScraper. Two viable shapes:
  1. **New module** src/psp_etl/scrape/gigabyte_server.py that imports helpers (_HEADERS, _CDN_HEADERS, throttling) from gigabyte.py and overrides the catalog URL/socket detection.
  2. **Generalise** GigabyteScraper to accept a catalog-URL list and socket-detection regex, then register two CLI entries (gigabyte-consumer, gigabyte-server). Cleaner long-term, more invasive.
- Recommend (1) initially; revisit (2) if Aspeed BMC firmware scraping is later added (similar structure).
- BIOS ZIPs for MZ-boards typically contain a raw .ROM/.BIN plus an EFI flash utility — same _extract_rom logic as consumer should work.

License-safe references: none in the surveyed prior art covers Gigabyte server.

Acceptance criteria:
- Class at src/psp_etl/scrape/gigabyte_server.py
- Tests: catalog parse + per-board BIOS list + fixture ZIP extraction
- classify_board_class returns EPYC for SP3/SP5/SP6 (already wired)
- CLI registration

Related: #79, #81.
